narrativeReportMd:
# Group R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found. The highest-impact local change is the replacement of R4's mandatory `Group.actual` boolean with R6's mandatory coded `Group.membership`, plus the removal of `Group.active`. R6 also expands Group into a canonical-style cohort definition resource with richer membership criteria.

## Scope
The analysis compared the local R4 and R6 core `StructureDefinition-Group.json` files and related local terminology artifacts. Inherited `Resource`/`DomainResource` changes, search parameters, operations, profiles, and IG-specific behavior were excluded.

## Main migration themes
R4-to-R6 migration requires an explicit transform for `actual` to `membership` and a policy for `active` to `status`. R6-to-R4 conversion is substantially lossy for conceptual/enumerated/definitional membership, expanded type codes and member targets, non-AND characteristic combinations, and new characteristic qualifiers. R6 model/code generation must also handle CanonicalResource-style metadata and new modifier elements.

## Highest-impact findings
The hard instance breaks are `Group.actual` removal/replacement by required `Group.membership` and removal of `Group.active` when populated. The highest backward-compatibility risks are expanded `Group.type`, expanded `Group.member.entity` targets, and modifier `Group.combinationMethod`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for mapping R4 `actual` and `active`, interpreting legacy `Group.code`, and deciding how to handle R6 Groups that use conceptual membership, new type codes, new member targets, or non-all-of characteristic logic.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several R6 changes are probably justified by richer cohort-definition needs, but some could have been staged less disruptively by retaining deprecated R4 elements or using extensions during transition.

## Follow-up analysis
A cross-version ConceptMap or implementation policy for Group-specific mappings would materially improve migration safety. Terminology expansion and standalone narrative/spec diff review would improve confidence for value-set and semantic-text details.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 keeps the `Group` identity but changes the local model in breaking ways: mandatory R4 `actual` is replaced by mandatory `membership`, optional R4 `active` is removed, and R6 adds richer canonical and cohort-definition semantics. The largest migration concerns are membership-basis inference, lifecycle mapping, and lossy R6-to-R4 conversion for expanded types/targets and characteristic logic. The main uncertainty is the absence of an official Group cross-version ConceptMap or narrative diff.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Treat migration as a semantic transform, not a field rename. `actual=true/false` cannot be mapped to `membership` without understanding whether membership is enumerated, definitional, or conceptual. `active` needs a local policy for `status`. R6-to-R4 conversion should detect and either extension-preserve or reject new type codes, new member targets, canonical metadata, `valueExpression`/`valueUri`, non-`all-of` combination methods, and characteristic qualifiers such as `offset`, `duration[x]`, and `relativeTime`.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural deltas because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared, and key terminology CodeSystems/ValueSets were inspected locally. Confidence is lower for intended migration mappings and justification because no official diff narrative, ballot rationale, terminology-server expansion, or cross-version ConceptMap was available.

findings.title: Mandatory Group.actual boolean was replaced by mandatory Group.membership code

oldState.summary: R4 required Group.actual as a 1..1 boolean.

semanticText.definition: If true, the resource refers to a specific group of real individuals. If false, the group defines a set of intended individuals.

constraints.human: Can only have members if group is "actual"

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 uses a required boolean, `actual`, to distinguish a real enumerated group from a descriptive/intended group. The R4 root invariant also ties the presence of `member` to `actual = true`.

newState.summary: R6 removes Group.actual and requires Group.membership as a 1..1 code.

binding.description: The basis for membership in a group

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: No R4 counterpart code system exists for this element; the R6 codes split the old boolean into membership-basis concepts.

semanticText.definition: Basis for membership in the Group, distinguishing definitional, conceptual, and enumerated groups.

constraints.human: Group.type SHALL be defined if Group.membership is either 'definitional' or 'enumerated'

newState.narrativeMd: R6 replaces the boolean with a required coded element. `enumerated` means membership is determined by listed members; `definitional` and `conceptual` mean characteristics are necessary and sufficient, with `conceptual` allowing no FHIR-bound `type`.

facts.note: Element added in R6 and is mandatory.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `Group.membership` inherits the same requirement rationale as R4 `Group.actual`, but it is not a lossless rename: the R6 code distinguishes `definitional`, `conceptual`, and `enumerated`, while R4 had only true/false.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct instance break. Every conformant R4 Group must carry `actual`, which is not a valid R6 element, and no R4 instance can already contain the mandatory R6 `membership` element. A converter must remove `actual`, infer a membership code, and add it. The inference is not mechanically lossless because `actual=true` may mean an enumerated list or a known subset of a definitional group, and `actual=false` may become either `definitional` or `conceptual` depending on whether `Group.type` remains meaningful.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrectly classifying a cohort as enumerated versus definitional changes who is considered a member and can affect cohort analytics, eligibility, and access-control logic.

justification.inferredGoal: Replace an overloaded boolean with explicit membership semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `actual` while adding `membership` as the preferred explicit membership-basis element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable: a three-code membership basis is clearer than the R4 overloaded `actual` boolean. A less-breaking staged design could have preserved R4 instances, but it would have left consumers reconciling `actual` and `membership`, and old boolean-only data would still be semantically weaker. Those material tradeoffs make the breaking replacement probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep R4 `actual` as deprecated and add `membership`, allowing legacy instances to validate while encouraging new R6 producers to populate the richer code. That would preserve most R4 data and still introduce the new concept, but the duplicated same-resource representation could persist indefinitely and create ambiguity when both fields are present or when only `actual=false` is available.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances, but leaves overlapping membership representations and does not force legacy data to carry explicit R6 semantics.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Group.actual` as min 1, max 1, type boolean.
R4 permits members only when `actual = true`.
R6 defines `Group.membership` as min 1, max 1, type code, with required membership-basis binding.
R6 membership-basis codes are `definitional`, `conceptual`, and `enumerated`.

examples.examplesMd: The example illustrates the core break: the R4 fragment contains the mandatory `actual` element and no `membership`; the R6 migration must choose a membership code, here `enumerated` because listed members determine membership.

findings.narrativeMd: `Group.actual` is not preserved in R6. It is replaced by `Group.membership`, a required code that distinguishes several membership bases. This affects validation, generated model classes, FHIRPath expressions, search logic, and business rules that used `actual` as a simple true/false flag.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid Group with `actual` is invalid against the R6 core StructureDefinition because `actual` is unknown and `membership` is missing. Conversely, an R6-valid Group with `membership = conceptual`, `definitional`, or `enumerated` cannot be represented exactly by the R4 boolean without losing information.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Migration must populate `membership` explicitly. A reasonable but review-dependent starting rule is: groups whose listed members define membership map to `enumerated`; characteristic-defined cohorts map to `definitional`; groups whose kind cannot be bound to FHIR resource types map to `conceptual`. Preserve the original R4 `actual` in an extension or audit trail when the inference is uncertain, and test cases with members, characteristics, both, and neither.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is semantically valuable but could have been staged more compatibly by retaining `actual` as deprecated. Because R6 makes the new code mandatory and removes the old boolean, a lossless automatic transform is not always possible.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: No local R4-to-R6 ConceptMap for `actual` to `membership` was found in the package inputs.

findings.title: Group.active was removed while R6 adds lifecycle status as an optional modifier element

oldState.summary: R4 has optional `Group.active` boolean, with missing meaning generally active.

semanticText.definition: Indicates whether the record for the group is available for use or retained for historical purposes.
semanticText.meaningWhenMissing: This resource is generally assumed to be active if no value is provided for the active element.

oldState.narrativeMd: `active` was a simple record-availability flag. When absent, R4 generally assumed the group was active.

newState.summary: R6 has no `Group.active`; it adds optional `Group.status` using publication-status codes and marks status as a modifier.

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

flags.isModifierReason: Applications should not use a retired Group without due consideration.

semanticText.definition: The current state of this Group.

newState.narrativeMd: `status` is part of the R6 canonical-definition pattern. It is optional but is a modifier; consumers must consider values such as `retired`.

facts.newValue: no equivalent default stated on Group.status

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `status` is the nearest R6 lifecycle-state element, but it is not a direct rename of `active`; it has more values and different canonical-artifact semantics.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance that includes `active` is not valid as an R6 Group without transformation. R6 `status` values such as `draft` and `unknown` have no exact R4 boolean representation, and `retired` only loosely resembles `active=false`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Lifecycle-state mistakes can cause retired or inactive cohorts to be used in decision support, reporting, or cohort operations.

justification.inferredGoal: Align Group with canonical resource lifecycle metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `active` as a deprecated R6 element while adding canonical-style `status`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Aligning Group with canonical-resource lifecycle metadata is a reasonable R6 goal, but removing the R4 `active` field was not necessary to accomplish it. Keeping the boolean while adding `status` would have preserved populated R4 instances and allowed R6 systems to move toward the richer lifecycle code. The remaining tradeoff is moderate rather than enough to require a hard removal.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base design could retain `Group.active` with its R4 meaning, mark it deprecated, add optional `Group.status`, and define how to interpret or warn on combinations such as `active=false` with `status=active`. This preserves old data while supporting canonical metadata. The downside is duplicate lifecycle representation that might linger, but that is a lower-cost compatibility burden than invalidating all R4 instances that populated `active`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Creates overlapping lifecycle fields and possible inconsistency, but the conflict is manageable with deprecation, mapping guidance, and status precedence.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Group.active` as 0..1 boolean with meaning-when-missing.
`Group.active` is absent from the R6 Group snapshot.
R6 defines `Group.status` as 0..1 code, required binding to publication-status, and isModifier=true.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example maps `active=false` to `status=retired`, but that is a policy decision rather than a guaranteed semantic equivalence.

findings.narrativeMd: `Group.active` disappeared from the R6 resource. Systems that store active/inactive cohorts as R4 Groups must transform or preserve that information elsewhere. The closest R6 field, `status`, has canonical-publication semantics and is a modifier.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 data with `active` becomes R6-invalid unless the element is removed. R6 data with `status=draft`, `status=retired`, or `status=unknown` can be reduced only approximately to an R4 boolean.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define a site policy before conversion: commonly `active=true` maps to `status=active`, `active=false` maps to `status=retired`, and missing `active` may map to omitted `status` or `active`. Keep original values in an extension if record availability and publication lifecycle are distinct in the source system.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change aligns Group with R6 canonical resource conventions, but the old element could have remained as a deprecated alias to preserve instance compatibility.

findings.title: Group.type is no longer always mandatory and the required group-type value set was expanded

oldState.summary: R4 requires `Group.type` 1..1 and binds it to six group-type codes.

binding.description: Types of resources that are part of group.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 code system contains person, animal, practitioner, device, medication, and substance.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 always requires the group to declare a FHIR resource-type category.

newState.summary: R6 makes `Group.type` 0..1 but conditionally requires it unless membership is conceptual; its required value set includes many more codes.

binding.description: Types of resources that are part of group.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The old six R4 codes are still present; R6 adds codes and allows no `type` only when `membership = conceptual`.

constraints.human: Group.type SHALL be defined if Group.membership is either 'definitional' or 'enumerated'

newState.narrativeMd: R6 broadens the allowable group categories and creates conceptual groups that need not be tied to a FHIR resource type.

facts.note: New root invariant conditionally requires type.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The change is not an R4-to-R6 hard break because R4 instances already have `type` and the old required codes remain in R6. It is a significant R6-to-R4 risk: conceptual Groups can omit `type`, and Groups using newly added type codes fail R4 required-binding validation.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrectly collapsing new type categories can distort group membership validation and downstream resource-target assumptions.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow Groups over more resource kinds and conceptual groups not bound to FHIR resource types.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: R6 widens `type` and preserves the R4 codes, so this is not an R4-to-R6 instance break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of supporting conceptual groups and more group member categories is reasonable, and the observed change does not reject R4-valid `Group.type` values. The breakage described here is mainly for R6 content that cannot be represented in R4, not for migration of R4 instances into R6.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because the R4 required codes remain valid in R6 and the cardinality is relaxed, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable under the R4-to-R6 base-design calibration. Extensions or code suppression for backward exchange would be R6-to-R4 mitigation, not a less-breaking R6 base design for preserving R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed; the cost is R6-to-R4 down-conversion for conceptual groups and new codes.

evidence.detail: R4 `Group.type` is 1..1 with required binding to group-type|4.0.1.
R6 `Group.type` is 0..1 with required binding to group-type|6.0.0-ballot4 and condition grp-2.
R6 group-type adds careteam, healthcareservice, location, organization, relatedperson, specimen, medicinalproductdefinition, substancedefinition, biologicallyDerivedProduct, and nutritionProduct.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example is valid with no `type` only because `membership` is `conceptual`; R4 requires `type` and has no conceptual membership basis.

findings.narrativeMd: `Group.type` moved from an unconditional required discriminator to a conditionally required one, and the required code system was expanded substantially. The old codes are not removed, so forward validation of R4 data is not the problem; backward conversion of new R6 categories is.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6: no hard break from this element alone. R6-to-R4: missing `type` and newly added codes are invalid under R4 cardinality and required terminology binding.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 transforms, reject or extension-preserve conceptual Groups without `type`. For new type codes, do not coerce them into old broad categories unless a business-approved ConceptMap exists; otherwise preserve the original code in an extension and flag the record.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The expansion is intrinsically incompatible with R4 required terminology. A backward-compatible R4 representation would require extensions or profiles rather than a base-code mapping.

findings.title: Group.member.entity accepts many new target resource types in R6

oldState.summary: R4 member references are limited to Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Device, Medication, Substance, and Group.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 member target profiles align with the six R4 group-type categories plus nested Group.

newState.summary: R6 retains old targets and adds CareTeam, HealthcareService, Location, Organization, RelatedPerson, Specimen, MedicinalProductDefinition, SubstanceDefinition, BiologicallyDerivedProduct, and NutritionProduct.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 aligns member references with the expanded group-type value set.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Widening target profiles does not invalidate R4 instances in R6. It does create a hard backward-validation failure for R6 Groups whose members reference newly allowed resource types, because R4 validators and generated models restrict the target set.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping or coercing members during backward conversion can change the actual cohort membership.

justification.inferredGoal: Support Groups over the expanded set of R6 member categories.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding reference targets preserves all R4 member references.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The target expansion follows directly from the broadened R6 Group type model and does not invalidate any R4 instance. A design that kept only R4 targets would preserve backward exchange but would fail the R6 goal of first-class Groups over the newly supported resource kinds.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No R4-to-R6 compatibility alternative is needed because R4 target profiles are retained. Carrying the new targets only in extensions would be a down-conversion workaround and would make the R6 base model less useful for standard validation, search, and member processing.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is backward conversion of new R6 target types, not R4-to-R6 compatibility.

evidence.detail: R4 target profiles are Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Device, Medication, Substance, and Group.
R6 target profiles include the R4 targets plus ten additional resource types.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 member reference to Organization is valid in R6 but outside the R4 target profile set.

findings.narrativeMd: `Group.member.entity` is substantially widened. R4 implementations often generate enumerated reference target types or validation switches; those will not accept many R6 member references.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 references remain valid in R6. R6 references to new target types are not R4-representable as core `Group.member.entity` values.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For backward conversion, detect new target resource types before serializing to R4. Use extensions or reject with a clear error rather than silently omitting members. Update R6 client code, validators, and search/indexing logic to handle the larger target set.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is a necessary consequence of expanding Group beyond the R4 member categories. R4 compatibility cannot be preserved without making the new references non-core extension content.

findings.title: Group.code changed from member-kind example coding to extensible group-use coding

oldState.summary: R4 `Group.code` is 0..1 CodeableConcept with an example binding and member-kind semantics.

binding.description: Kind of particular resource; e.g. cow, syringe, lake, etc.

semanticText.definition: Provides a specific type of resource the group includes; e.g. "cow", "syringe", etc.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 uses `code` to specialize the kind of members, with no computable value set URL in the binding.

newState.summary: R6 `Group.code` is still 0..1 CodeableConcept but has an extensible binding to group-code and describes the use of the Group.

binding.description: A code that describes the kind of group, which usually dictates what kind if entities can be in the group.

semanticText.short: Use of the Group (and by implication, kind of members)
semanticText.definition: A code that describes the use of the group. The use of the group usually dictates what kind of entities can be members of the group.

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 value set includes use-case codes such as `patient-list`, `family`, `household`, `herd`, `locality`, and `collection`.

facts.oldValue: specific type of resource the group includes

impact.impactRationaleMd: Base FHIR extensible bindings usually do not make all out-of-set codes invalid, so this is not a universal hard validation break. However, R6 validators and profiles can now expect use of the group-code value set when applicable, and code that interpreted R4 `code` as member-kind may make wrong decisions in R6.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify Group use cases and provide a standard extensible vocabulary.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain R4 `code` as member-kind coding and add a new optional group-use element bound to `group-code`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A standard vocabulary for Group use is a reasonable goal, but changing the semantics and binding expectations of the existing `code` element was not the only way to achieve it. A new optional group-use element would have preserved R4 interpretations while enabling the R6 vocabulary with relatively modest long-term cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would leave `Group.code` focused on the kind of members, as in R4, and add a separate optional element such as `Group.use` for the R6 group-use vocabulary. This would preserve R4 business rules and validation behavior. The tradeoff is one additional element and possible overlap during adoption, but it avoids forcing implementers to reinterpret old `code` values.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds another classifier and may slow convergence, but avoids repurposing an existing element with established business meaning.

evidence.detail: R4 `Group.code` has example binding and member-kind definition.
R6 `Group.code` has extensible binding to ValueSet/group-code and group-use definition.
R6 group-code includes use-case concepts such as patient-list, family, household, herd, exposure-group, locality, organization, and collection.

examples.examplesMd: The example illustrates semantic migration, not a guaranteed required mapping: an R4 member-kind text such as `cow` may need to become R6 group-use coding plus other descriptive detail.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes `Group.code` from a loose member-kind descriptor into a more standardized description of how the Group is used. Existing code systems, enum switches, and analytics that rely on R4 semantics need review.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances are not automatically invalid merely because their code is outside the R6 extensible value set, but R6 conformance tooling can raise stronger issues than R4. The larger risk is behavioral: the same element name now carries different modeling intent.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit uses of `Group.code`. Map source codes to the R6 group-code value set when there is a clear equivalent; otherwise preserve original coding/text and consider adding a local extension or profile guidance. Update business rules to distinguish group type, group use, and member characteristics.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The more compatible design would have added a new group-use element while retaining the old member-kind role for `code`. R6 chose a simpler base model at the cost of semantic migration work.

findings.title: R6 adds modifier Group.combinationMethod for combining characteristics

oldState.summary: R4 has no combinationMethod; all characteristics are implicitly combined as all-of/AND.

semanticText.comment: All the identified characteristics must be true for an entity to a member of the group.

oldState.narrativeMd: Multiple R4 characteristics are conjunctive: every listed characteristic must hold.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional modifier `Group.combinationMethod` and optional `Group.combinationThreshold`.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 ValueSet includes five required codes; the CodeSystem also contains additional concepts not included in this ValueSet.

flags.isModifierReason: Changing the combinationMethod from all-of to any other value changes the interpretation of multiple characteristics.

semanticText.definition: Used to specify how two or more characteristics are combined.
semanticText.meaningWhenMissing: If absent, this element is treated as though it had been set to 'all-of'.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can express OR, at-least-n, at-most-n, and exclusion-subset combinations that R4 could not express as core content.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 data without `combinationMethod` migrates safely to the R6 default of `all-of`. The risk is in R6 processing and backward conversion: `combinationMethod` is a modifier, so ignoring it can invert cohort membership logic, and non-`all-of` combinations cannot be faithfully represented in R4.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Cohort inclusion/exclusion logic can change materially if OR or threshold combinations are ignored.

justification.inferredGoal: Support richer characteristic logic for cohort definitions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: this is optional R6 content with an R4-compatible default of `all-of`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Richer characteristic combination logic addresses a real expressivity gap, and marking the element as a modifier is appropriate because non-default values change cohort semantics. Since omitted `combinationMethod` retains R4 all-of behavior, this is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: An extension-only approach could carry OR or threshold logic for backward exchange, but that would hide safety-critical semantics from generic R6 processors. Under the calibration rules, that is not a backward-compatible base alternative for preserving R4 instances; it is a lower-visibility mitigation for R6-to-R4 representability.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy for non-`all-of` logic, but R4 instances migrate without needing a less-breaking base alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 says all identified characteristics must be true.
evidence.quote: All the identified characteristics must be true

evidence.detail: R6 adds `Group.combinationMethod` as 0..1 code, required binding, isModifier=true.
R6 adds `Group.combinationThreshold` for at-least/at-most methods.

examples.examplesMd: R4 would interpret two characteristics as requiring both A and B; the R6 example means A or B.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 makes the characteristic combination rule explicit and more expressive. This is a runtime-sensitive change because a modifier element can change the meaning of every characteristic in the Group.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is not broken because missing `combinationMethod` defaults to `all-of`. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy for any non-`all-of` value. Strict R6 processors must include the modifier in semantic evaluation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Initialize migrated R4 Groups with omitted `combinationMethod` or `all-of`. For R6-to-R4, reject non-`all-of` combinations or preserve them with extensions and clear warnings. Add tests that compare membership evaluation for all-of, any-of, at-least, at-most, and except-subset.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The default preserves R4 behavior, but adding the modifier creates new R6 content that R4 cannot model. A profile/extension approach would be more backward-compatible but less safe for generic processors.

findings.title: Group.characteristic.value[x] adds uri and Expression choice types

oldState.summary: R4 value[x] allows CodeableConcept, boolean, Quantity, Range, or Reference, with an example value binding.

binding.description: Value of descriptive member characteristic; e.g. red, male, pneumonia, Caucasian, etc.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 characteristic values are concrete concepts, booleans, quantities/ranges, or references.

newState.summary: R6 value[x] keeps the R4 types and adds uri and Expression; the R4 example binding is no longer present on value[x].
newState.narrativeMd: R6 can express a characteristic value as a URI or as a formal Expression, enabling algorithmic or externally identified criteria.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding choice types is not a forward validation break, but it affects generated class hierarchies, serializers, FHIRPath, and switch statements over the choice element. R6 `valueUri` and `valueExpression` cannot be represented in R4 core `value[x]` without extension or transformation.

justification.inferredGoal: Support externally identified and expression-based membership criteria.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding `uri` and `Expression` choice types preserves R4 `value[x]` instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Supporting URI-identified and expression-based criteria is consistent with the R6 Group definition use case. The change widens the type domain and does not remove or narrow any R4 value choice, so the compatibility question is limited to new R6 content and implementation updates.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is applicable because existing R4 choice values remain valid. Extensions could have carried URI or Expression criteria, but that would be an interoperability tradeoff for R6 producers rather than a way to preserve old R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The cost is generated-code and down-conversion handling for new R6 choices, not R4-to-R6 instance breakage.

evidence.detail: R4 allows CodeableConcept, boolean, Quantity, Range, and Reference.
R6 adds uri and Expression to the choice type list.

examples.examplesMd: The `valueExpression` choice name is R6-only for Group.characteristic.value[x]; R4 has no equivalent choice type.

findings.narrativeMd: The R6 choice expansion is mostly a backward-conversion and code-generation issue. Existing R4 values still fit, but R6 producers can now emit value types older clients do not recognize.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is not broken. R6-to-R4 validation fails for `valueUri` or `valueExpression` because those element names are not valid R4 choices.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update generated models and serializers for the two new choices. For R6-to-R4, preserve URI or Expression values in extensions or reject the conversion if semantic fidelity is required. Include choice-type coverage in tests.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional choice additions are forward-compatible but not backward-compatible. Extensions would be more backward-compatible but less interoperable for R6 consumers.

findings.title: R6 adds several characteristic qualifier elements, including modifier offset

oldState.summary: R4 characteristic has code, value[x], exclude, and period only.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 can say what characteristic value applies, whether to exclude it, and the calendar period over which it is tested.

newState.summary: R6 adds description, method, formula, determiner, offset, instances[x], duration[x], and relativeTime under characteristic.
newState.narrativeMd: The new fields add natural-language description, determination method, derivation formula, determining party, value offset, occurrence count, duration, and relative timing. `offset` is a modifier because it changes how the value is interpreted.

facts.newValue: grp-1: Ranges have to be positive

impact.impactRationaleMd: These are optional additions, so they do not invalidate R4 data in R6. They are material for R6 consumers because `offset` is a modifier and the added qualifiers can change membership evaluation. R4 has no core slots for this information.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Ignoring offset, duration, instances, or relative timing can make a cohort criterion materially broader or narrower than intended.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent richer evidence-grade and temporal criteria for Group membership.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: the qualifier elements are optional additions that do not invalidate R4 characteristics.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The added qualifiers support more precise cohort and characteristic definitions, and they are optional for migrated R4 instances. The modifier status on `offset` is justified by its effect on value interpretation. This is therefore an additive R6 expressivity change, not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design choice.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Using extensions for these qualifiers would help backward exchange but would make important R6 criteria less visible to generic processors and validators. Because R4 instances do not need those extensions to remain valid in R6, `backwardCompatibleAlternativeAvailable` is not applicable for this calibration.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 conversion can lose qualifier semantics, especially modifier `offset`, but R4-to-R6 validation is preserved.

evidence.detail: R4 local characteristic children are code, value[x], exclude, and period.
R6 adds eight characteristic children including modifier `offset` and constrained `instances[x]`.
R6 `offset` has isModifier=true with reason that it must be included to interpret the characteristic value.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 characteristic uses `offset` and `durationDuration`, neither of which exists in R4 Group.characteristic.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 characteristic criteria are much richer. This is useful but can surprise R4-era processors that assume only code/value/exclude/period need to be evaluated.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 instances remain valid with respect to these additions. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy whenever any added qualifier is populated. Ignoring `offset` is especially unsafe because it is a modifier.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update R6 evaluators to process or reject the new qualifiers explicitly. For R6-to-R4, use extensions for each qualifier or fail the conversion. Include tests for offset, formula, relativeTime, duration, instances Range, and method/determiner handling.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The additions could be extension-only for R4 compatibility, but the base R6 model benefits from making the qualifiers visible and machine-processable.

findings.title: Group now implements CanonicalResource-style metadata

oldState.summary: R4 Group is a DomainResource without CanonicalResource implementation and lacks canonical metadata elements such as url/version/title/publisher/useContext/purpose/copyright.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 Groups are ordinary resources with identifiers and descriptive elements, not canonical conformance artifacts.

newState.summary: R6 Group declares structuredefinition-implements CanonicalResource and adds many optional canonical metadata elements.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds `url`, `version`, `versionAlgorithm[x]`, `title`, `status`, `experimental`, `date`, `publisher`, `contact`, `description`, `useContext`, `purpose`, `copyright`, and `copyrightLabel` as local Group elements.

facts.newValue: cnl-1 warning: URL should not contain | or #

impact.impactRationaleMd: The added metadata elements are optional, so R4 instances do not become invalid in R6 because of them. R6 instances that use canonical metadata cannot be serialized as R4 Group without data loss, and generated R6 model classes gain many fields and a CanonicalResource interface expectation.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow Group to serve as a reusable canonical definition artifact.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: CanonicalResource metadata is optional R6 content and does not invalidate R4 Group instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing Group to serve as a reusable canonical definition artifact is a coherent R6 goal, and adding optional metadata is the least disruptive base-model path for R4-to-R6 validation. The compatibility concerns are generated-class changes and down-conversion of R6 metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A separate artifact or extension-only metadata could reduce generated-field growth, but it would split workflows or make canonical identity less standard. Since the added fields are optional and preserve R4 instances, those are design tradeoffs for R6 functionality rather than backward-compatible alternatives to a breaking change.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is additional R6 model surface and lossy R6-to-R4 exchange, not a need for a less-breaking R4-to-R6 design.

evidence.detail: R4 Group has no structuredefinition-implements CanonicalResource extension.
R6 Group implements CanonicalResource.
R6 adds canonical metadata elements including url, version, status, date, publisher, useContext, purpose, and copyright.

examples.examplesMd: R4 Group has no core `url`, `version`, or `status` elements; those values require extensions or a companion artifact when down-converting.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 broadens Group from an instance-oriented resource to one that can also behave like a canonical definition. This is mostly additive, but it affects generated interfaces, summary views, search expectations, and R6-to-R4 conversion.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is not broken by optional additions. R6-to-R4 conversion loses canonical metadata unless extensions are used. Strict R4 parsers reject the new element names.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate R6 models and update serializers to include the new fields. For R6-to-R4 exchange, define extensions or external metadata storage for canonical fields. Treat `status` as a modifier as described in the separate active/status finding.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional metadata additions are the least disruptive way to make Group canonical in R6, but any use of the new fields is inherently outside R4 core.

findings.title: Group.characteristic and key children became summary elements

oldState.summary: R4 `Group.characteristic`, `.code`, `.value[x]`, and `.exclude` are not summary elements.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 summary responses do not include the characteristic backbone by default.

newState.summary: R6 marks `Group.characteristic`, `.code`, `.value[x]`, and `.exclude` as summary elements.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 summary responses may include core characteristic criteria.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Summary flags do not affect instance validity. They can affect REST `_summary` behavior, generated summary projections, indexing payload size, and privacy assumptions about what appears in summary views.

justification.inferredGoal: Expose membership-defining criteria in summary views.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: summary flags affect runtime response shape, not R4-to-R6 instance validity.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Characteristics are central to interpreting an R6 Group, so including them in summary views is a reasonable goal. The change can surprise clients that depend on R4 summary payload shape, but it does not make R4 instances invalid or create an R6 base-design break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less disruptive operational choice would be to leave the summary flags unchanged and rely on `_elements` or profiles when callers need criteria. That is a runtime behavior alternative, not a backward-compatible base instance-design alternative under this calibration, because no R4 instance compatibility is at stake.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Leaving flags unchanged would preserve R4-style summary behavior but would make R6 summaries less informative for Group definitions.

evidence.detail: R4 characteristic summary flags are false.
R6 characteristic, code, value[x], and exclude summary flags are true.

examples.examplesMd: A server honoring R6 summary flags may include characteristic data in `_summary=true` responses where an R4-oriented client did not expect it.

findings.narrativeMd: The summary-flag change is not a validation break, but it can change API payloads and generated summary models. Systems using summaries for lightweight or low-sensitivity views should review expectations.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4 instance becomes invalid and no R6 instance becomes unrepresentable solely because of summary flags. The risk is runtime behavior of summary serialization and query responses.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review REST `_summary`, `_elements`, caching, and UI summary handling. If characteristic data is sensitive in a deployment, use access-control or projection rules rather than assuming summary mode omits it.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This could have been avoided by leaving flags unchanged, but including characteristic criteria in summaries is consistent with their central role in R6 Group semantics.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id/name, kind, type, derivation, abstract flag, and DomainResource baseDefinition are unchanged. The CanonicalResource implementation and maturity/status changes are captured as local findings/notable changes rather than an identity break.

No material cardinality change was found for unchanged local paths such as `identifier`, `name`, `code`, `quantity`, `managingEntity`, `characteristic`, `characteristic.code`, `characteristic.value[x]`, `characteristic.exclude`, `characteristic.period`, `member`, `member.entity`, `member.period`, or `member.inactive`. Cardinality changes involving `actual`, `membership`, and `type` are captured in findings.

Types are unchanged for most continuing elements, including `identifier`, `name`, `code`, `quantity`, `managingEntity`, `characteristic.period`, `member.period`, and `member.inactive`. `characteristic.value[x]` type additions are captured separately.
`Group.managingEntity` target profiles are unchanged. `Group.member.entity` target widening is captured as a finding.

No old required `Group.type` code was found removed; the R4 group-type codes remain present in R6. Binding changes for `type`, `code`, `membership`, `combinationMethod`, and characteristic-related elements are captured in findings.

No continuing local element had an in-place tightened R4 constraint. The R4 root `grp-1` actual/member rule is replaced by R6 root `grp-2`, and the new `characteristic.instances[x]` positive Range constraint applies only to a new R6 element.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value change was found for Group elements.

No maxLength, minValue, or maxValue change was found on continuing local elements. The new positive Range rule on `Group.characteristic.instances[x]` is captured with the new characteristic qualifier finding.
No existing local element changed from non-modifier to modifier in place. New modifier elements `Group.status`, `Group.combinationMethod`, and `Group.characteristic.offset` are captured in findings.
No local slicing was found on Group elements in either StructureDefinition snapshot.

The resourceType remains `Group`; no rename or split was found. Serialization/codegen risks are limited to added/removed fields, choice type expansion, canonical metadata, and summary/modifier flags captured in findings.

Major semantic text changes were reviewed and captured for root definition, `actual`/`membership`, `code`, characteristic combination, and new characteristic qualifiers. Some standalone narrative-page nuance may be missing.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Group maturity/status metadata advanced in R6 ballot build
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: StructureDefinition status and standards-status/FMM changes do not directly affect instance validity.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R4 Group was draft/trial-use/FMM 1; R6 Group is active/normative/FMM 3 in the inspected ballot package. Governance and conformance expectations may change even when instance wire format is not directly affected.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional member involvement coding
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `Group.member.involvement` is optional and absent from R4, so it does not invalidate R4 instances in R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 data that uses member involvement cannot be represented in R4 core. Family/household or role-sensitive Groups may need extensions for backward exchange.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 supplies an example value set for characteristic codes
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The binding remains example strength, so this is not a hard validation constraint for base instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 tooling may present or prefer `ValueSet/example-characteristic-codes`; local code systems should be reviewed for display/mapping quality.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 root definition adds family/household exceptions and performer/owner guidance
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The narrative broadens explanatory guidance rather than adding a computable validation rule.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Business rules that categorically disallowed Group acting collectively should review the new Patient/RelatedPerson family and household guidance.
